plain: Charles Buhler, who worked in NASA's electrostatics lab, tells Michels that he first saw unexplained forces in his experiments in 2010. After two years working with a colleague he names only as Drew, he thought the push came from momentum stored in electric and magnetic fields being turned into ordinary motion, which he calls "conversion... from field momentum to mechanical momentum without static charges," and they tested it after his wife pointed this out. He says it was only in 2018 that he "realized that I didn't even need the current," meaning static charge alone could produce thrust. If true, it would be a way to push a craft with no fuel thrown out the back, which the episode calls antigravity propulsion.
